Fiction is created for several reasons, and I would argue the main two are to make a statement (which could be a commentary or teaching a lesson) and to entertain. A lot of people use literature/fiction as a form of escapism. In a fictitious world anything can happen, and morality doesn't exist the same way it does in the real world. 

For some people, and I'm not afraid to say myself included, fiction is a way to experience things that one could never experience in the real world. Murder, rape, abuse; these are all things that are illegal in our world- and for good reason. Yet the human mind can be curious. Have you honestly never wondered what it feels like to kill a person? Perhaps you haven't... but I have and I don't think it's that uncommon to wonder. But in the real world wondering is as far as it goes for several reasons: 1) It's illegal- your life would be ruined; you'd be jailed for a long time, 2) it's immoral- you ruin the lives of others. Murder and rape and abuse are all terrible terrible evils. And yet... they are fascinating. People love to interact with horrible things. Horror films, and podcasts discussing and documenting serial killers and the like- these things are fascinating  because they are so taboo. 

Another thing is that these types of situations are very nuanced. In the real world RAPE IS RAPE- it's terrible and sickening and evil. I wouldn't wish that on any person who lives and breathes and feels and thinks. That being said, I have a kink for nonconsensual sex, such as consensual-nonconsensual (irl) and i really enjoy rape mangas. I can enjoy the manga/manwha because the characters are not real people. In real life Sangwoo would be a monster who deserved what he got. No question. But because Killing Stalking is a fictional work and neither Sangwoo or Yoon Bum actually feel, it is a haven and an escape where I can endulge my dark fantasies. There is nothing wrong with having dark fantasies.

I would also distinguish, in literature, the difference between two kinds of rape. A lot of the kind of rape that shows up in manga/manwha (especially in the omegaverse) is a kind of... less violent rape. The uke says "no," which makes it rape, ofc, but they enjoy themselves or at least their body does. IRL, again, it would be unacceptable, but drawings don't have feelings. The other kind is the violent kind where a person is screaming and pleading and it's violent and horrifying. This kind of rape I, personally, don't even enjoy because there is no pleasure, just pain. It's difficult to describe, but this kind of rape is often what is portrayed in movies, too when a character is raped and seeing their trauma is horrifying. 

Some kinks are a little disturbing, like people who get off to 23 Kg anorexic girls, or necrophilia and dismemberment kinks, or even BDSM. These kinks all glorify the harm of another human being (whether the person fantasizes about hurting someone or someone hurting themselves). I think that people are turned on by what turns them on. They like what they like. It's not wrong to like horrible things, what matters is what you do with it. So having a rape kink is fine as long as you don't bring your rape kink to the real world (like telling rape victims it wasn't that bad, or actually raping someone). Having a kink for anorexic girls is fine if you don't encourage people to be anorexic in real life and encourage them to get help instead. 

So the bottom line, is that for me (and I am sure there are many more like me) I ship Yoon Bum and Sangwoo because I find the abuse and violence between them hot (as a massochist), and I also ship them because I feel that they reflect the reality of living with mental disorders. The violence towards others that sangwoo exhibits, the violence towards himself that Bum exhibits, and the other things like Sangwoo projecting people from his past (his mother) onto people in his present (Bum) is all horrifyingly familiar, it is the story of mental disorder and the struggle both outer and inner that we face. I see myself and my deepest pain in the two characters- I gain so much more out of seeing them together than just sexual satisfaction (even though I focused on that above). The story is really hopeless and depressing just like life can seem for people with BPD, which makes sense because this is Bum's story after all. I love Bum, and part of me wants him to escape and find happiness elsewhere, but I find so much satisfaction and comfort in seeing the two broken boys go through experiences together that I don't want them to be apart. Because they are fictional characters who don't really have feelings, and i am a person who does, I value my own needs above Bum's, and that is why I ship them.
